feature_request: Project managers should be able to see the full history of engagement with a country before starting a new mission.

proposed_scope_in.item: Read-only 'Engagement History' tab on the existing Country record, showing a reverse-chronological timeline of existing Engagement records for that country (date, type, summary, contact, linked Mission/Project, logged-by).

Pre-mission checkpoint: when a Project Manager opens the 'Create Mission' flow and selects a Country, show the last 5 Engagements and a link 'View full history' that opens the Country Engagement History tab. It is informational only and does not block creation.
Basic filters on the timeline over existing fields only: date range, engagement type, and linked Mission/Project.
Visibility enforced by the existing Country/Mission access model: a Project Manager sees only the engagement records they can already see today. No new roles, flags or per-country settings.
Each timeline entry shows the contact name, linked from the existing Contact record. The timeline renders the contact's current role and status as stored, and does not backfill historical roles.
Paginated timeline (page size 25) with server-side query on the existing Engagement table via an index on (country_id, engagement_date). No new tables.

proposed_scope_out: Any new data-entry fields or forms for Regional Coordinators; the history only reads what is already logged
Mandatory acknowledgement, approval or gating step before a mission can be created
AI/automated summaries, sentiment or relationship scoring of engagement history
Historical backfill or cleaning of legacy engagement records; data is shown as-is
Point-in-time contact role/title history (valid_from/valid_to); current contact details are shown only
Cross-country or regional aggregate views and exports (CSV/PDF)
Per-record or per-country sensitivity flags and custom RBAC; any change to data classification is a human policy decision
Alerts or notifications about stale or missing engagement history
Editing engagement records from the history view

assumptions.statement: 'Full history' means all Engagement records already linked to the Country (directly or via its Contacts, Missions and Projects), not a new history log or audit trail.
assumptions.rationale: Reusing the existing Engagement entity needs no new table and no new data entry, so the feature is a read-only view that can ship in one release.

assumptions.statement: Existing engagement data is sufficiently complete and consistently linked to Country that a timeline is useful as-is; gaps are shown, not fixed.
assumptions.rationale: Cleanup or backfill would be an open-ended data project. Showing existing data keeps scope bounded and adds zero Regional Coordinator workload.

assumptions.statement: Project Managers need the history surfaced at the moment they start a mission (a summary in the create-mission flow), and informing them is enough; no gating or sign-off is required.
assumptions.rationale: A passive summary with a link delivers the 'before starting a mission' value without approval workflows or queues anyone must maintain.

assumptions.statement: Project Managers' current read access to Country, Mission and Engagement records is the right visibility boundary for this feature; whether any engagement content needs tighter classification is a policy question outside this MVP.
assumptions.rationale: Inheriting existing permissions avoids a new RBAC system and avoids creating a data-exposure path that bypasses current rules.

assumptions.statement: Showing the contact's current name/role/status from the Contact record is acceptable for history entries, even if the role has changed since the engagement.
assumptions.rationale: Point-in-time role tracking would need new columns and maintenance; a current-state link is sufficient for v1 situational awareness.

success_criteria.criterion: For 100% of countries, the Country Engagement History tab loads the first page (25 entries) in under 2 seconds at p95 on production-scale data.
When a Project Manager selects a country in the Create Mission flow, the last 5 engagements are shown without extra clicks, and 'View full history' is reachable in one click.
Zero new required fields or forms are added for Regional Coordinators, verified by schema and UI review before release.
In access testing, 0 engagement records are visible to a Project Manager through the history view that are not visible to them through existing Country/Mission screens.
Within 60 days of release, at least 60% of newly created missions have the country's history tab or panel viewed in the same session, measured via view-event logging.

challenges.challenge_text: A Project Manager on a Mission in Country X inherits 'current read access' to Country, Mission and Engagement records. Today that access is likely scoped per mission or screen, and engagement notes are scattered across records. A 'full history' timeline aggregates every Engagement for the country in one view, including engagements logged against other missions, other ministries and prior coordinators. A PM can then read sensitive summaries (for example a ministerial dispute or a back-channel contact) from engagements on missions they were never assigned to. The criterion 'visible through existing screens' does not test this, because existing screens never presented the aggregate. Least-privilege needs an explicit rule: the history is filtered by the viewer's mission or country assignment at query time, not just by Country-level read permission, and the summary text is covered by the same filter. The cross-mission case needs a test.
challenges.evaluation_of_proposer: The Proposer defers to existing permissions and calls classification a policy question. That is only valid if the existing model is per-record and enforced server-side on the aggregated query. This has not been shown, and the first-5 panel in Create Mission is a new exposure path before any mission assignment exists.

challenges.challenge_text: Each timeline entry links to the Contact's current name, role and status. When a minister or ministry official is replaced, a 2022 engagement with the 'Minister of Trade' will display the new minister's name and title, or a deactivated or blank contact. A PM could then believe the current minister was engaged on a past sensitive topic, or contact a departed official, and so misread the relationship history and send the wrong message. Without at least a snapshot of name/role as logged (contact_name_at_time) or a visible 'contact since changed / inactive' badge, the history silently misleads under the turnover this CRM faces. A badge needs no new tables.
challenges.evaluation_of_proposer: The Proposer explicitly accepts the staleness and only descopes point-in-time history. The cheaper mitigation, flagging contacts whose role/status changed after the engagement date, was not considered.

challenges.challenge_text: The Proposer assumes engagement data is complete and consistently linked to Country, with gaps simply shown. Engagements linked only via a Contact, Mission or Project (A1) may have no direct country_id, and the index on (country_id, engagement_date) will not return them. A PM looking at the timeline for Country X sees a quiet history and concludes no prior engagement, when a recent difficult meeting was logged under a contact or mission without country_id. This false sense of 'nothing happened' leads to a mission launched without context. An empty or sparse timeline needs an explicit caveat, and the query must match the A1 definition of linkage (direct or via Contact/Mission/Project), or the definition must be narrowed.
challenges.evaluation_of_proposer: A1 defines history as direct or indirect linkage, but the scope item only indexes country_id. The two are inconsistent, and the assumption of completeness is untested with no data-quality check before release.

challenges.challenge_text: The pre-mission checkpoint shows the last 5 engagements whenever a PM selects a country in Create Mission, and success is measured by 60% of new missions having history viewed. The 'last 5' are purely recency-ordered, so routine low-value logs (scheduling emails) can push out the one important engagement. With no signal of significance or of how stale the latest entry is, PMs learn to skim past the panel. Also, the panel fires before the PM has any assignment to the country or mission. Selecting a country in the dropdown should not display engagement summaries for countries the PM does not work on. The panel needs the same access filter as C1 and a 'last engagement was N months ago' cue so it conveys useful information.
challenges.evaluation_of_proposer: The Proposer treats the panel as passive and harmless. Passive does not mean safe: it is a new disclosure surface at mission creation, and a panel people learn to ignore does not meet the 60% view metric's intent.

challenge_responses.response: The risk is real, and the fix is cheap: it is a rule on the query, not a new model. The history tab and the Create Mission panel now apply the existing per-record access predicate server-side to the aggregated query, with summary text under the same filter. A cross-mission test and a no-access-country test are now success criteria. I am not inventing a new assignment-based rule. Whether PMs should see engagements on missions they were never assigned to is an access/classification policy decision for a human owner. If the existing model turns out to be only Country-level read, that policy question must be routed to the security/data-classification owner before release, and this feature should not widen exposure beyond today's per-record rules.

A derived badge is cheap: it is a read-time check on the existing Contact status field, with no new column, table or data entry. The contact column is now labelled as current role, and a 'Contact now inactive' badge appears when the linked Contact is inactive or departed. I am deliberately not adding a contact_name_at_time snapshot: a new column would only populate going forward and could not fix the legacy history PMs are reading. I am also not adding a 'role changed' badge based on last-modified dates, since phone or email edits would create frequent false positives. If PM feedback shows role-change confusion on active contacts, add point-in-time role history in a later release.

The Critic is right that the A1 definition and the original query were inconsistent. The fix is cheap: the query now follows the A1 linkage (direct country link, or via Contact, Mission or Project) with de-duplication, backed by indexes on existing link columns. Always-on static caveat text says an empty or sparse history does not mean no contact. A pre-release data check reports how many engagements link to a country only indirectly or not at all, so the completeness assumption is measured rather than assumed. I am not adding backfill or cleanup, since that is an open-ended data project. Engagements that resolve to no country by any path will remain invisible, and the caveat covers that residual risk.

Two parts are adopted because they are cheap. (1) The panel uses the same server-side access filter as C1 and shows a neutral message with no counts or summaries when nothing is permitted, so selecting a country in the dropdown discloses nothing the PM cannot already see. (2) A derived 'Last engagement: N months ago' cue computed from the latest permitted engagement date conveys staleness without any new data. I am DEFENDING the cut on significance ranking: it would need either a new importance field, which means Coordinator data entry, or a scoring model, and both are out of scope. The residual risk of routine logs crowding the 5-item panel is bounded because the full filterable timeline is one click away. If view-through rates on the panel fall short of the 60% criterion, or PM feedback shows important engagements being missed, consider an engagement-type filter default in a later release.

challenges.challenge_text: Engineering has done its part: the existing per-record access predicate is now applied server-side to the tab and the Create Mission panel, summary text is covered, and cross-mission and no-access-country tests are success criteria. What remains is whether the existing predicate is the right boundary. If it only grants Country-level read, a PM could read sensitive summaries from missions they were never assigned to, such as a ministerial dispute or a back-channel contact. Only a security or data-classification owner can decide that.
challenges.evaluation_of_proposer: The Proposer correctly declines to invent an assignment-based rule and commits to not widening exposure beyond today's per-record rules. It also commits to routing the policy question to the security owner before release. That is the right division of labor. The remaining disagreement is institutional access policy, not an engineering gap.

final_decision.feature_request: Project managers should be able to see the full history of engagement with a country before starting a new mission.
final_decision.executive_summary: V1 adds a read-only Engagement History tab on the Country record. It shows a paginated, filterable timeline built from existing Engagement records, found by direct or indirect linkage to the country, with a 'Contact now inactive' badge, a contact column labelled as current role, and an always-on caveat that a sparse history does not mean there was no contact. The main trade-off argued was how cheaply the Critic's concerns about misleading history and data exposure could be met without new data entry, tables or gating. Contact staleness, incomplete linkage and the panel's staleness cue were resolved (C2, C3, C4) with derived or read-time fixes. The pre-mission checkpoint in Create Mission and server-side per-record visibility enforcement are pending a human decision on C1, and so is the access-testing success criterion. That decision is whether the existing access predicate is the right visibility boundary for aggregated engagement history.

surfaced_assumptions.resolution_notes: C2 challenged showing current contact details on historical entries. The Proposer added a 'Contact now inactive' badge and a current-role label, and the Critic accepted, so the assumption was revised and accepted.

open_questions_for_humans.decision_owner: Unassigned: product owner to route (likely the security or data-classification owner)
open_questions_for_humans.question: Engineering cannot decide this access policy. The history tab and Create Mission panel will reuse the existing per-record read predicate for Engagement and Mission records, summary text included, and will add no new assignment-based rules. Is that predicate an acceptable visibility boundary for an aggregated country history, which could let a Project Manager read sensitive summaries from missions they were never assigned to, such as a ministerial dispute or back-channel contact? Or must access be restricted further by a policy owned by a human? The answer determines whether the pre-mission checkpoint, server-side visibility enforcement and the access-testing criterion can proceed.
